Estimate L curves for two groups of images

Source: R/MiSA_estimate.R
estimate_L.Rd

Estimates Ripley's \(L\)-function for each taxon of interest, across all images in two groups (e.g., health vs. disease), over a pre-specified sequence of radii.

Usage

estimate_L(
  groupA_image_list,
  groupB_image_list,
  taxa,
  r_vec,
  groupA_window_list = NULL,
  groupB_window_list = NULL,
  border_correct = "border"
)

Arguments

groupA_image_list

A named list of data frames representing the images in group A. Each data frame must contain the columns x, y, and taxon_name, representing the x and y spatial coordinates and the corresponding taxon identity, respectively.

groupB_image_list

A named list of data frames representing the images in group B, with the same structure as groupA_image_list.

taxa

A character vector giving the taxa of interest for which the \(L\)-function will be estimated.

r_vec

A numeric vector giving the sequence of radii at which the \(L\)-function will be evaluated. This set of radii is used consistently across all images.

groupA_window_list

(optional) A named list specifying pre-defined study regions (observation windows) for the images in groupA_image_list. Each element must be an object of class owin, as required by the window argument of spatstat.geom::ppp(). Names must match the corresponding image names in groupA_image_list. A window may be specified for some images and left as NULL for others. If NULL is provided (either for a single image or the entire list, the default), the function derives a convex hull from the data as the default window.

groupB_window_list

(optional) A named list specifying pre-defined study regions for the images in groupB_image_list, with the same structure and default behavior as groupA_window_list.

border_correct

(optional) Character string specifying the edge correction method used when estimating the \(L\)-function. One of "border" (the default), "iso", or "trans". For spatial microbiome data, "border" is recommended, as the other two options substantially increase computation time.

Value

A list containing the estimated \(L\) curves for each image and taxon.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
r_all <- seq(0, 1500, by = 6)
taxa_all <- unique(healthImg.list[[1]]$taxon_name)

L_result <- estimate_L(groupA_image_list=healthImg.list, groupB_image_list=diseaseImg.list,
taxa=taxa_all, r_vec=r_all,groupA_window_list = NULL, groupB_window_list = NULL,
border_correct = "border")
} # }
